What each column is, what you can edit, and where the data runs out

VORP and Rapid VORP

VORP is the season-long version: xPts above the (teams × slots + 1)-th best player at that position — the body you could still get once everyone has filled their squad. It answers "how much is he worth over the whole draft".

Rapid VORP answers the question you actually have with the clock running: what does waiting one round cost me here? The baseline is not the end of the draft but the best players at his own position whose ADP says they will still be there at your next pick. Set whether that baseline is the best 1, 2 or 3 of them. A high Rapid VORP means the position falls away sharply right after him; near zero means someone just as good is likely to survive the round, whatever his season-long VORP says. Hover the cell for the baseline it used.

Both recompute when you edit anything — and note that Rapid VORP also moves when you edit somebody else's ADP, because that changes who is still on the board.

BD Pick, and the round Pick value judges him in

BD Pick is the second column and it ships empty. Put in the overall pick number you would actually spend on a player — 1 to 120 in this league — and Pick value starts judging him in that round instead of the round his ADP implies. Nine in an eight-team league is round two. Clear the cell and it goes back to ADP.

The reason for the column: ADP is an average of what other people's leagues did, which answers when will he come off the board. That is the right question for There at and Rapid VORP, and both still use ADP for exactly that reason. It is the wrong question for Pick value, which needs to know when you would spend a pick, because that is what decides whether his downside is unaffordable or his upside is free. Nobody but you can supply that, which is why it is a blank column rather than a default.

What it changes: before the crossover round a player is marked down toward his Floor, after it he is marked up toward his Ceiling, and at the crossover he is scored flat on xPts. So a volatile player is punished as an early pick and rewarded as a late one — same projection, different question. Hover a Pick value cell to see which round it used and where the number came from.

BD Picks are saved in this browser along with your other edits, and Reset edits clears them — it will warn you first. Nothing re-runnable can rebuild them, because they are yours.

Editing and columns

Eight things are editable: BD Pick, xMins adjusted, Mins/start, xG/90 mine, xA/90 mine, Role, Transfer threat and ADP. The four rate ones re-score the player using the same arithmetic as xpts_calc.py, not an approximation of it.

The rates you can change sit in their own columns. xG/90 and xA/90 are the model's, greyed and untouchable; xG/90 mine and xA/90 mine start equal to them and are yours. So the original is always readable next to the change, and xG season and xA season follow whatever you set, multiplied by your minutes.

That matters most for the 119 summer arrivals: their minutes are researched but their rates are empty, because nothing in the Premier League data can supply them. These are the cells to fill in from what you know about what they did elsewhere.

Every edit shows in a darker blue with a ↶ that puts that one field back to the model's number. Edited by me filters to the rows you have touched, and Reset edits clears the lot.

Drag any column header sideways to move it; the order saves too. The number and the player name stay pinned at the left so a wide table still reads. Reset columns puts them back.

The leftmost column is the row's place in the current sort, and clicking it puts that player on your research list — outlined for no, filled for yes. Shade my pick rows then shades the rows landing on your picks in the snake: 4, 13, 20, 29 for slot 4 of 8, not every fourth row, because the turn reverses each round so the gap alternates between 9 and 7. It follows whatever order the table is in, so sorting it your way shows where your own picks fall.

Draft slot and bands

Set your slot and league size and My picks lists your overall pick numbers in a snake. There at is the last of those picks a player is still projected to be available at, read off ADP. gone means his ADP is earlier than your first pick. Edit an ADP and the bands and Rapid VORP both move. This is arithmetic on other people's draft behaviour, not a view about any player, and it does not choose anyone. BD Pick deliberately does not feed these two: what you would do cannot make a player survive to your next pick.

ADR Pros

The mean rank a player is given by published draft rankings from named analysts — 259 players carry one. Only whole-draft lists count toward it. Position-by-position lists are deliberately excluded: the Premier League's own Scout publishes four separate rankings, so its four number ones are the best goalkeeper, the best defender, the best midfielder and the best forward, and averaging those against a global top 100 makes the best keeper look like the best player alive.

Every row behind this column was re-fetched and checked against its source by scripts/verify_pro_rankings.py before being used, because the tooling that collected it produced a complete, plausible, entirely invented ranking for a URL that returns a 404. Four rows that could not be traced back to what was actually published are excluded.

Role and transfer threat

Role comes from the club research, which named a starter and his competition for every position at 17 clubs. nailed and likely are the researcher's words for the starter; contested means the slot is in the fight; rotation means he was listed as competition for someone else's place; unknown means the research did not reach him. Transfer threat is whether the club is still shopping for that position (reinforcement) or willing to sell him (exit).

Set pieces — and the gap

Corners is the share of his club's 2025/26 corners he actually took, measured rather than assumed, and the closest thing to a left/right split: a first-choice taker on 40% or more is taking both sides.

Free kicks and penalties can only be an order, never a percentage. Nothing in any source counts free kicks or penalties taken, only who is designated. FPL also publishes a single combined order for corners and indirect free kicks, so the indirect free-kick taker cannot be told apart from the corner taker at all.
